のときに.en: とき by itself means "when"・"at the time when", not "every time".  However, if you add "はいつも" you will get "ときはいつも" which is one of proper ways to say "every time".

のとき.en: とき by itself means "when"・"at the time when", not "every time".  However, if you add "はいつも" you will get "ときはいつも" which is one of proper ways to say "every time".

おきに.en: おきに is a suffix that is attached to things such as numbers and counters, highlighting that something happens 'every (A)', or 'at intervals of (A)'. We're looking for a grammar point that is paired with either verbs or nouns to express something happens 'whenever (A)', or 'each time (A)'.

たびに.en: A particle must be used when this structure follows a noun.

attributes.translation: Every time I get a medical check up, some kind of illness is discovered. I wonder if it has to do with my age.
attributes.nuance_translation: An expression that states that something happens every (A), where the focus is on the unique occurrence or degree of (A).

attributes.body_ja:
「度（たび）に」は、名詞（めいし）「度（たび）」の副詞的（ふくしてき）な形（かたち）です。動詞（どうし）や名詞（めいし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われて、「(A) のときはいつも (B)」や「(A) するときは、毎回（まいかい） (B)」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

「たびに」が名詞（めいし）と使（つか）われるときは、間（あいだ）に格助詞（かくじょし）「の」が必要（ひつよう）です。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「たびに」は「ごとに」のように「毎（まい）〜」という意味（いみ）を持（も）ちますが、動作（どうさ）や出来事（できごと）に対（たい）して使（つか）われます。回数（かいすう）を表（あらわ）すときには使（つか）われません。
attributes.body:
度（たび）に is the adverbial form of the noun 度（たび）, meaning 'time' (as in 'at the time of'). たびに is frequently paired with either verbs, or nouns, in order to show that something happens 'whenever (A)', or 'each time (A)'.

After nouns, the case marking particle の will be required before たびに.

Fun Fact

Like ごとに, たびに means 'every'. However, たびに is most often used to convey the nuance of するごとに 'every time doing'. Due to this, たびに will almost always be used to highlight some kind of action or event, rather than random amounts of time.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: ごとに and たびに both express frequency, and can be interchangeable in cases like 失敗するたびに／ごとに 'every time (you) fail'. However, ごとに can directly follow time or distance expressions (e.g. ３時間ごとに), while たびに requires a verb indicating an action or event, e.g. ３時間が経つたびに 'every time 3 hours pass'. Their noun forms also differ, e.g. 発表の度に vs. 発表ごとに (both meaning 'with every announcement').

Both おきに and たびに describe repeated occurrences, but are used differently. おきに attaches to time expressions to mean 'at intervals of (A)', e.g. '５分おきに電車が来る' ('Trains arrive every five minutes'). たびに describes a response that recurs whenever a particular thing happens, e.g. '見るたびに笑ってしまう' ('I end up laughing every time I see it').

first_relatable.title: おきに
first_relatable.meaning: Repeated at intervals, Every other, Every, At intervals of

attributes.body: These are similar expressions that both express the idea that every time one thing happens, so does something else. While they are interchangeable in some cases, につけ can only be used for naturally occurring events, e.g. '見るにつけ笑ってしまう' ('I laugh every time I see it'). たびに can also be used for volitional actions, e.g. '出張に行くたびにお土産を買う' ('I buy souvenirs every time I go on a business trip').

Both まい～のように and たびに express frequency and the idea of 'every,' but with different nuances. まい～のように is used with 'every~' time expressions to mean 'almost every (A)', e.g. 毎日のように 'almost every day'. In contrast, たびに follows verbs or noun phrases to mean 'every time (A)', e.g. 彼に会うたびに 'every time I see him' or 旅行のたびに 'every time I take a trip'.

first_relatable.title: まい～のように
first_relatable.meaning: Almost every ~, Nearly every ~, On a ~ basis
